title.narrative: Smart Water Management for Surface Water and Groundwater

description.narrative: In response to growing water demand and environmental pressures, river basin organisations are required to adopt a conjunctive approach to managing surface and groundwater, termed “smart water management.” This approach seeks to optimise and sustainably balance water resources to meet future needs. Integrating surface and groundwater management is unconventional in Indonesia, as responsibilities are divided between the Ministry of Public Works (surface water) and the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (groundwater). To address this, Indonesian stakeholders have proposed a Smart Water Management System (SWMS) to foster cooperation, improve data availability, and support evidence-based policy for water distribution, spatial planning, and land use.The initiative is driven by rising bulk water demand from rural, industrial, and agricultural sectors, coupled with uncontrolled groundwater extraction causing land subsidence and coastal erosion, particularly in Northern Java. Semarang and surrounding areas have been selected as a pilot site. In this project, a reconnaissance phase was conducted in which local stakeholders were actively engaged to build consensus and define SWMS requirements. Currently, data on water resources, user demand, and development impacts is fragmented, limiting integrated planning. The SWMS aims to enhance strategic decision-making for long-term water allocation and reduce groundwater extraction, rather than manage daily operations. Stakeholders demonstrated commitment but emphasised the need for alignment with strategic planning and a lead partner. The Ministry of Public Works integrates the outcomes of this project in the forthcoming World Bank GRASS project.
